fields.why: The mean age at introduction (5.7 months) is a single descriptive mean, never compared across groups or interpreted; every claim rests on weighted percentages of early introduction. Under v5 that does not make the outcome continuous.

The methods give a blanket 'two-sample t-tests ... across subgroups', and the results are one level against the others (Black vs each other group; bachelor's degree, mothers aged 30-39 and >=400% FPL vs all other levels). V6(a)/(f) make that per-group vs referent only. Nothing says every pair was tested, and the FPL note's second referent (<100% vs 200-399% and >=400%) still leaves pairs unreported.

brief_issues: The brief does not say how to read a result whose notes name two or more referents but report only some pairs (here FPL). A rule could say: 'pairwise (all pairs)' only when the article states or shows every pair; otherwise per-group vs referent only.
